recipes.description: Alcatra is a traditional beef stew from Terceira Island in the Azores, Portugal, known for its rich, slow-cooked meat with spices and wine.
instructions: Cut the beef into large chunks and marinate with garlic, bay leaves, red wine, vinegar, salt, and pepper for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Heat olive oil in a heavy pot or traditional clay pot over medium heat.
Brown the marinated beef chunks on all sides until sealed and caramelized, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté chopped onion and garlic until translucent and fragrant.
Return the beef to the pot and add sliced chorizo, remaining marinade, and enough water or beef broth to cover the meat.
Add bay leaves and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover the pot and simmer on low heat for about 2 to 3 hours until the beef is tender and the sauce thickens.
Towards the end of cooking, add peeled baby potatoes and allow them to cook until tender.
Adjust seasoning if necessary and remove bay leaves before serving.
recipes.name: Alcatra Beef Stew (Terceira Island)

recipes.description: American beef stroganoff is a creamy and comforting dish made with sautéed beef strips, mushrooms, and onions in a sour cream sauce, traditionally served over egg noodles.
instructions: Slice the beef into thin strips and season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the beef strips and cook until browned on all sides, then remove from the skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, melt butter and add chopped onion and sliced mushroom.
Cook until the vegetables are soft and browned.
Add minced garlic and cook for another minute.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir to combine, cooking for one minute to remove the raw flour taste.
Slowly pour in beef broth while stirring to avoid lumps, then add mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until slightly thickened.
Return the beef and any juices to the skillet and reduce heat to low.
Stir in sour cream and heat gently without boiling to combine.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot over cooked egg noodles or rice, garnished with chopped parsley if desired.
recipes.name: American Beef Stroganoff

recipes.description: A traditional Mexican mixed roast combining pork shoulder and beef chuck marinated in spices, beer, and orange juice, then slow-cooked until tender and flavorful.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cut the pork shoulder and beef chuck into large chunks about 5 cm each.
In a large bowl, combine the pork and beef with minced garlic, chopped onion, chopped bell pepper, chili powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. Mix well to coat all the meat evenly.
Add the diced tomato and pour in the orange juice and beer. Mix everything together, then marinate covered in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours, preferably overnight.
In a large heavy oven-safe pot or Dutch oven, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Remove the meat from the marinade reserving the liquid. Brown the chunks of pork and beef in batches, ensuring all sides are golden. Transfer browned meat to a plate.
Add the chopped onion and bell pepper to the pot and saute until translucent.
Add the marinade liquid back into the pot and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the browned meat to the pot, cover with a lid, and transfer the pot to the preheated oven.
Roast for about 2 to 3 hours or until the meat is tender and easily shreds with a fork, basting occasionally with the cooking liquid.
Once cooked, remove the pot from the oven, shred or cut the meat into smaller pieces, and mix with the juices before serving.
recipes.name: Asado De Puerco Y Res (Mixed Pork and Beef Roast)

recipes.description: Avignon Beef Daube is a traditional Provençal slow-cooked beef stew simmered in red wine with aromatic herbs and vegetables, resulting in tender, flavorful meat typical of southern France.
instructions: Cut the beef into large cubes and marinate with red wine, crushed garlic, chopped onion, sliced carrot, sprigs of thyme, bay leaves, and crushed black pepper for at least 12 hours, preferably overnight, in the refrigerator.
Remove the beef from the marinade and pat dry, reserving the marinade and vegetables separately.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add chopped onion, sliced carrot, and minced garlic; cook until softened and fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir to coat, cooking for about 2 minutes to eliminate the raw taste.
Return the beef to the pot along with the reserved marinade, including the herbs and vegetables, and add tomato paste and a pinch of salt.
Bring the mixture to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat for about 3 hours until the beef is very tender, stirring occasionally and adding water if necessary to keep the meat partially submerged.
Towards the end of cooking, add chopped black olives and chopped fresh parsley, then adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve the daube hot, traditionally accompanied by crusty bread, mashed potatoes, or pasta.
recipes.name: Avignon Beef Daube (Provençal Beef Stew)

recipes.description: Traditional Texas-style smoked BBQ beef brisket flat with a flavorful dry rub and tender, juicy texture, perfect for a smoky main dish.
instructions: Preheat the smoker or grill to 110°C (225°F).
Trim excess fat from the brisket flat, leaving about 0.5 cm of fat for moisture.
In a small bowl, mix salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and paprika to create the dry rub.
Apply a thin layer of yellow mustard over the brisket flat to help the rub adhere, then coat the brisket evenly with the dry rub mixture.
Place the brisket flat fat side up on the smoker or grill and smoke for about 4-5 hours, maintaining a steady temperature of 110°C (225°F).
After the initial smoking, wrap the brisket tightly in aluminum foil or butcher paper to retain moisture.
Continue cooking for another 2-3 hours until the internal temperature reaches 90°C (195°F).
Remove the brisket from the smoker and let it rest wrapped for at least 1 hour to redistribute the juices.
Slice the brisket flat thinly against the grain and serve with your choice of BBQ sauce.
recipes.name: BBQ Beef Brisket Flat

recipes.description: BBQ Beef Brisket Point is a tender and flavorful cut of beef slow-smoked with a savory rub, popular in American barbecue, known for its smoky crust and juicy texture.
instructions: Trim excess fat from the beef brisket point, leaving about 1/4 inch of fat for flavor and moisture.
Mix salt, black pepper, paprika, garlic powder, and brown sugar to create a dry rub.
Apply the dry rub evenly over the entire surface of the brisket point, pressing it into the meat.
Preheat the smoker to 110°C (225°F) using hardwood like hickory or oak for smoke flavor.
Place the brisket point fat side up on the smoker grate and smoke for approximately 6 hours, maintaining a steady temperature.
Spritz the brisket every hour with a mixture of apple cider vinegar and water to keep it moist.
After 6 hours, wrap the brisket point tightly in aluminum foil or butcher paper to retain moisture.
Continue smoking the wrapped brisket for an additional 4 to 6 hours, or until the internal temperature reaches 95°C (203°F) and the meat is tender.
Remove the brisket from the smoker and let it rest, still wrapped, for at least 1 hour at room temperature.
Unwrap the brisket and slice across the grain into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Serve with your favorite barbecue sauce and side dishes like coleslaw or baked beans.
recipes.name: BBQ Beef Brisket Point

recipes.description: Grilled beef sausages brushed with smoky barbecue sauce, perfect for a simple and flavorful outdoor meal.
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
Prick the beef sausages a few times with a fork to prevent bursting during cooking.
Place the sausages on the grill and cook for about 10 to 12 minutes, turning occasionally to ensure even cooking and grill marks.
During the last few minutes of cooking, brush the sausages with barbecue sauce to add flavor and caramelize the exterior.
Once cooked through and slightly charred, remove the sausages from the grill.
Serve hot with additional barbecue sauce on the side, accompanied by your choice of sides such as grilled vegetables or bread rolls.
recipes.name: BBQ Beef Sausage

recipes.description: Slow-cooked BBQ beef short ribs that are tender and flavorful, coated in a rich, smoky barbecue sauce perfect for a hearty main dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F).
Season the beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the short ribs on all sides until a deep crust forms, about 2-3 minutes per side, then remove and set aside.
Add chopped onion, garlic, and bell pepper to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, smoked paprika, chili powder, brown sugar, and stir for 1-2 minutes to combine.
Add barbecue sauce, beef broth, and apple cider vinegar to the pot, stirring well.
Return the short ribs to the pot, ensuring they are partially submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot with a lid and transfer to the oven.
Cook for 3 to 3.5 hours or until the meat is tender and falling off the bone.
Once cooked, remove ribs from the pot and set aside.
Simmer the sauce on the stove to reduce and thicken if desired.
Serve the short ribs topped with the thickened sauce and garnish with chopped parsley.
recipes.name: BBQ Beef Short Ribs

recipes.description: Barbacoa de Res is a traditional Mexican slow-cooked beef dish made with tender, marinated brisket cooked in a flavorful chile sauce until it easily shreds. It is perfect for tacos, burritos, or as a hearty main course.
instructions: Soak dried guajillo and ancho chiles in hot water for about 15 minutes until soft, then drain.
Place softened chiles, chopped onion, garlic, ground cumin, dried oregano, ground cloves, apple cider vinegar, beef broth, salt, and pepper in a blender. Blend until smooth to make the marinade.
Cut beef brisket into large chunks and place in a large bowl.
Pour the chile marinade over the beef, making sure all pieces are well coated. Marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight in the refrigerator.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear the marinated beef chunks on all sides until browned, then remove from the pot.
Add chopped onion and garlic to the pot, sauté until translucent.
Return the beef to the pot, pour in remaining marinade and beef broth if necessary to cover meat halfway.
Add bay leaves to the pot and bring to a low simmer.
Cover the pot tightly and cook on low heat for 4 to 5 hours until beef is very tender and shreds easily.
Remove beef from the pot and shred with two forks, discarding any excess fat and bones.
Return shredded beef to the pot, mix well with the cooking juices, and heat through before serving.
recipes.name: Barbacoa De Res (Slow-cooked Beef)

recipes.description: Barbacoa de Res Hidalgo is a traditional Mexican slow-cooked beef dish from Hidalgo, known for its tender, flavorful meat infused with chilies and aromatic spices.
instructions: Cut the beef into large chunks suitable for slow cooking.
In a large pot, combine water, guajillo chili (seeded and soaked), garlic, onion, cloves, allspice, cloves, black pepper, cinnamon stick, oregano, and salt to create a flavorful cooking broth.
Blend the soaked guajillo chilies with garlic, onion, cloves, black pepper, cinnamon stick, oregano, and salt until smooth to form a marinade sauce.
Marinate the beef chunks in the chili sauce for at least 2 hours or overnight for deeper flavor.
Place the marinated beef and marinade into a large pot or oven-safe dish.
Add the cooking broth to cover the meat; bring to a boil and then reduce heat to a low simmer.
Cover the pot tightly and cook the beef slowly for 4 to 6 hours, or until it is very tender and easily shredded with a fork.
Once cooked, shred the beef into pieces and mix it with the cooking juices to retain moisture and flavor.
Serve the barbacoa hot with warmed corn tortillas, chopped onion, cilantro, lime wedges, and salsa as desired.
recipes.name: Barbacoa De Res Hidalgo (Hidalgo Style Beef Barbacoa)
